greetings: Bem-vindo to the jungle, my friend! Try not to step on the poison dart frogs.
Ah, an adventurer! Tell me, have you come to dance Capoeira, or just to steal our gold? I am fine with both.
The canopy sees all, knows all, and frankly, is quite unimpressed with your fashion sense.
guild_master.reward: Take this. It is a sacred relic of my ancestors. Also, I found it in a parrot's nest this morning.

farmer: I planted wheat, but the jungle said 'no' and gave me man-eating vines instead. I call it a win.
You haven't lived until you've tried my cocoa bean and melon smoothie. It will violently reset your digestive system.
Every day is a battle against the monkeys. They took my hoe. They took my dignity.
I am the master of the bamboo! Also, I have a bamboo splinter. Please help, it hurts so much.
I tried planting potatoes. The soil laughed at me. Literally, a mud spirit manifested and chuckled.
My watermelons are structurally sound enough to be used as siege ammunition.
Do not eat the glowing mushrooms. I did, and I spoke to a capybara about macroeconomics for three hours.
The key to a good crop is singing to it in Portuguese. If you sing in Spanish, the vines will strangle you.
Farming in the jungle is 10% planting and 90% aggressively machete-ing the overgrowth.
I respect the earth. The earth respects me. The giant spiders respect neither of us.
fisherman: Caught a piranha today! It cost me three fingers, but the soup will be worth it.
The pink river dolphins are majestic creatures. They also owe me 50 emeralds. If you see one, tell it I'm looking for it.
I don't use a fishing rod. I stare intensely at the water until the fish surrender out of fear.
Would you like to buy a catfish? It is the size of a small car and extremely angry.
The river provides. Mostly driftwood and old boots, but occasionally, a very confused salmon.
Never fish at midnight. The water reflects the stars, and the stars will ask you uncomfortable questions about your childhood.
I once hooked a squid, and it slapped me with all eight tentacles. We are married now.
You call this fishing? Back in my day, we wrestled the caimans for their lunch!
I am running out of bait, so I have started using shiny emeralds. It's not working, but I look very wealthy while failing.
Do not look into the depths. The depths are looking back, and they think your haircut is ridiculous.
shepherd: Sheep do not survive the jungle. I shear capybaras now. The wool is terrible, but they are very polite about it.
I tried to herd the ocelots once. The scars have mostly healed, but the emotional damage is permanent.
My llama spat on me. I spat back. We have been in a tense standoff for 47 hours.
Look at this beautifully dyed wool! The red comes from a flower, the blue from a berry, and the green from a frog that I am deeply afraid of.
If you find a sheep in the jungle, do not trust it. It is an imposter. A spy of the canopy.
I knit sweaters for the parrots. They hate them. I do it anyway.
The secret to a good shear is a steady hand and a profound acceptance of your own mortality.
I have trained my flock to dance the samba. It is mesmerizing, and slightly terrifying.
Wool is useless in this heat. I am sweating constantly. Why did I choose this profession?
Take care of the animals, and they will take care of you. Except the jaguars. They will just eat you.
fletcher: Bamboo arrows: fast, light, and almost guaranteed to give your enemy a nasty splinter.
I coated this arrowhead in tree sap. It won't kill them, but they will be very sticky and annoyed.
Fletching in this humidity is a nightmare. The feathers just turn into sad, wet clumps.
Do you want the poison dart or the really poison dart? The second one smells like mangoes.
I once shot an arrow into the air, and a parrot caught it and threw it back at me. I have never felt so disrespected.
A bow is a precise instrument. Therefore, I only use it to shoot fruit out of tall trees.
These arrows are perfectly balanced. The universe, however, is not. Embrace the chaos.
I don't sell crossbows. Too clunky. If you can't solve your problems with a swift piece of bamboo, you deserve to lose.
My finest arrows are fletched with macaw feathers. Don't tell the macaw, he is still looking for them.
Aim for the heart. If you miss, aim for the knees. If you miss that, run.
cleric: The ancient jungle temple calls to me! Mostly to tell me that I left the oven on.
I have deciphered the mossy cobblestone runes. They say: 'Send help, it is very hot.'
Do not touch the gold in the temple! It is cursed. I mean, I will buy it from you, but it is definitely cursed.
I bless this water with the power of the canopy! It is now 90% mud, but spiritually very cleansing.
The spirits of the jungle demand a sacrifice! A melon will do. Maybe two, I skipped breakfast.
Redstone traps are the universe's way of saying 'You should have stayed home today.'
I offer spiritual guidance and minor curse removal. For major curses, you will need a bucket of milk and a good lawyer.
The villagers think I'm crazy because I talk to the vines. The vines think I'm crazy because my posture is terrible.
Behold, the Eye of Ender! It is looking at me judgmentally.
We are all just dust in the wind. Sticky, humid, mosquito-bitten dust.
weaponsmith: A diamond sword is nice, but have you tried a machete? It cuts vines, it cuts cake, it cuts your enemies!
I forged this blade in the heart of a jungle fire. It is permanently lukewarm.
If you swing this axe hard enough, you might actually hit the mosquito that's been bothering you.
Axes are for trees. Swords are for monsters. This pointy stick I found is for poking things I don't understand.
The humidity rusts the iron faster than I can smelt it. My life is a tragedy of oxidization.
I don't just sell weapons. I sell solutions to 'I am currently being chased by a zombie' problems.
A good blade should sing when you swing it. Mine just makes a sad 'whoosh' noise.
This sword was blessed by a shaman. He charged me 5 emeralds, so I am charging you 15.
Do not lick the iron. I don't know why I have to say this, but the last adventurer tried to.
In the jungle, the best weapon is a loud voice and a fast pair of boots.
armorer: Turtle shell helmets! Stylish, eco-friendly, and you can hide in them if a creeper gets too close.
Wearing full iron armor in the jungle is like wearing an oven. I highly recommend it for my amusement.
I have crafted this chestplate to be highly breathable. Unfortunately, it is breathable because it is full of holes.
Leather armor rots. Iron rusts. Gold bends. Just fight naked, it's more intimidating anyway.
I will gladly repair your shield, but it will cost you. Mostly because I hate looking at it.
My armor is designed to deflect arrows, zombies, and the harsh realities of adult life.
I tried making armor out of bamboo. It worked perfectly until a panda ate it off my customer.
A strong defense is a good offense. I don't know what that means, I just hit things with a hammer.
Chainmail is just a heavy net you wear as a shirt. It is profoundly uncomfortable.
Protect your head, protect your heart. The rest of you is replaceable.
toolsmith: Need a shovel? No you don't, it's all mud. Just use your hands, you coward.
This pickaxe is guaranteed to break precisely when you find diamonds. It is cursed, but very cheap.
A good hoe is the foundation of a good farm. A bad hoe is just a stick with a metal bit that falls off.
I made a specialized tool for cutting vines. It's called a 'sword', but don't tell the weaponsmith I'm selling them.
Why do you need an axe? Just stare at the tree until it falls over in submission.
My tools are forged with precision, care, and a lot of swearing when I hit my thumb with the hammer.
You look like someone who breaks a lot of tools. I like you. We will do much business.
I don't sell 'flint and steel'. I sell 'portable arson devices'.
A tool is only as good as its user. In your case, this pickaxe is doomed.
Every tool has a purpose. Your purpose is to give me emeralds for this tool.
butcher: Churrasco time! I have beef, I have pork, I have something I found in a temple that I am afraid to identify!
You haven't lived until you've had my slow-roasted jungle chicken. The secret ingredient is spite.
I asked the farmer for a pig, he gave me a melon. I butchered the melon. It was very messy.
Do not ask where the meat comes from. Just close your eyes and chew.
I tried to make an ocelot stew once. The ocelots formed a union and now I have to pay them minimum wage.
Raw meat is for monsters. Cooked meat is for villagers. Burnt meat is for my mother-in-law.
I have a special today on 'mystery jerky'. It's chewy, salty, and possibly made of zombie.
A good butcher respects the animal. A great butcher respects the marinade.
My sausages are renowned throughout the biome! Mostly for their explosive properties.
Life is short. Eat the steak. Ignore the cholesterol.
leatherworker: Caiman skin boots! Perfect for wading through mud, completely useless for anything else.
I can make a saddle for a pig, a horse, or if you're feeling adventurous, a very large spider.
Tanning leather in this humidity is like trying to dry water with a sponge.
I made this item frame out of the finest leather. Please do not put dirt in it. It hurts my feelings.
A good pair of leather pants is essential for jungle survival. They chafe horribly, but you look fantastic.
I trade leather for emeralds. I trade emeralds for bread. I trade bread to the ducks. I have a problem.
Dyeing leather is an art form. My masterpiece is a brown tunic that looks slightly like a different shade of brown.
The cows look at me with such judgment. I just pretend I don't speak 'Moo'.
I will gladly fix your boots, but if I find mud in them, the price doubles.
Leather is versatile. You can wear it, you can craft with it, you can chew on it if you're really desperate.
mason: Mossy cobblestone isn't a design choice, it's just what happens if you leave a rock outside for five minutes here.
Chiseled stone bricks! I carved a little creeper face on this one. It took three hours and nobody notices.
I can make polished diorite, but I refuse to. Have some self-respect, buy granite.
The jungle temples are marvels of ancient masonry. And terrible ventilation.
You want to build a house out of wood in the jungle? Enjoy the termites, you absolute fool. Buy stone.
I stack rocks. I am very good at stacking rocks. Do not complicate my life.
Quartz is just fancy white stone that thinks it's better than everyone else. (I have some in the back, 10 emeralds).
I once tried to build a statue of myself out of mud. It rained. Now it is a puddle of myself.
A sturdy stone wall keeps the monsters out. It also keeps you in. It's a matter of perspective.
Rocks do not betray you. Rocks do not complain about the heat. Rocks are perfect.
cartographer: I have mapped the entire canopy! Actually, no, this is just a green smudge on a piece of paper.
Looking for the Lost City of Gold? Take this map. It leads to a swamp, but it will get you out of my hair.
Drawing maps in a jungle is useless. You take five steps, spin around, and everything looks exactly the same.
I can sell you a map to an ocean monument, but honestly, it's much drier here. Stay.
X marks the spot! Or it's a mosquito squashed on the parchment. Hard to tell.
My compass spins wildly. I think the magnetic pole is currently inside a very large parrot.
A map is a window to the world. A window you have to hold with both hands while running from skeletons.
I am a master of geography. For example, did you know we are currently surrounded by trees?
Do not fold the maps! Roll them! If you fold them, the crease will permanently alter the landscape. Probably.
The world is vast and full of wonders. I prefer to stay inside and draw little squares.
librarian: Welcome to the library! Please do not read the books. The humidity has glued all the pages together.
I have enchanted this book with 'Unbreaking III'. You'll need it, because the termites are relentless.
I tried to write a history of our village, but the paper turned to mush and the ink ran away.
Silence in the library! Tell that to the macaws outside, they are incredibly loud.
Knowledge is power. And in this case, power costs 24 paper and an emerald.
I have a rare ancient tablet here. It translates to 'Don't eat the yellow snow.' Very confusing, as it never snows here.
Books are the windows to the soul. Unfortunately, my window is covered in mold.
If you bring me a book and quill, I will write you a poem about how much I hate the humidity.
I sell bookshelves. They are mostly decorative, because actual books do not survive the jungle.
The pursuit of knowledge is a noble goal. The pursuit of a dry place to sit is a more practical one.
nitwit: CARNAVAL! Wait, is it Carnaval? I don't know, I just like wearing these feathers.
I stared at a frog for four hours today. The frog won the staring contest.
Everyone has a job. My job is to vibrate intensely when a thunderstorm starts.
I tried to invent a new dance, but I just fell over into a patch of sweet berries. It hurt, but the rhythm was undeniable.
The golems are my best friends. They don't talk much, but they are great listeners.
If you eat enough cocoa beans, you can see time. Or at least, you can see your heart beating out of your chest.
I'm not unemployed, I'm a 'freelance vibe consultant'. The vibes are currently very green.
Have you ever noticed that if you spell 'jungle' backwards, it doesn't make any sense? Deep stuff.
I lost my shoe in a puddle. I live in the puddle now. This is my home.
Hrrrm. Hrrrng? Haaaaah. (I am practicing my philosophical sighs).
none: I am currently looking for my purpose. So far, my purpose seems to be sweating profusely.
I could be a farmer, but I hate dirt. I could be a smith, but I hate fire. I am at a crossroads.
Do you have a job for me? I am highly skilled at complaining and taking naps in the shade.
I was going to get a profession today, but a monkey stole my motivation.
The jungle provides everything I need. Mostly heatstroke and mosquito bites, but it provides.
If you build me a lectern, I will become a librarian. Until then, I am simply a critic of the current administration.
Being unemployed is hard work. You have to actively avoid all the workstations.
I am practicing my 'harrumph' noise. It needs more bass, I think.
I am waiting for the economy to improve before I commit to a career path.
Perhaps tomorrow I will find my destiny. Today, I am going to watch the bamboo grow.

generic: It's not the heat that gets you, it's the humidity. And the zombies. Mostly the zombies.
A parrot repeated my deepest darkest secret today. I have never been more embarrassed.
Welcome to the jungle! We have fun and games. And a severe lack of air conditioning.
Did you hear that rustling in the bushes? It's either the wind, a jaguar, or Dave looking for his lost hoe.
If you see a temple in the distance, walk the other way. Trust me on this.
We are planning a massive festival! You are invited. Bring emeralds.
The canopy protects us from the sun, but it does nothing to stop the rain from ruining my hair.
I am saving up for a vacation to a snowy tundra. I want to know what 'cold' feels like.
Stay on the path. The path is muddy, miserable, and treacherous, but the jungle is worse.

greetings: I traded three cocoa beans for a shiny parrot feather, and honestly? Best financial decision of my life.
My big brother told me the Sun God will eat my toes if I don't finish my maize porridge. Is that true?!
I tried to climb the big step pyramid backwards, but the priest yelled at me for insulting the sky gods.
Have you seen my pet poison frog? His name is Squishy and he makes my skin tingle when I pet him!
I'm practicing for the sacred ball game! If I lose, mom says I have to clean the llama pens for a month.
The sun is super bright today! The Sun God must have had an extra big cup of hot cocoa.
I tried swinging on a jungle vine like a jaguar, but the vine was actually a snake. We were both very surprised.
My dad said cocoa beans grow on trees. I checked all the trees in the jungle and only found angry monkeys.
Do you have any shiny gold bits? I'm building a tiny pyramid for the leafcutter ants!
I learned how to carve stone today! Look, it's a turkey! ...Okay fine, it's supposed to be a creeper.
The temple priest said my aura is yellow today. I think that just means I ate too many mangoes.
I tried to challenge a macaw to a yelling contest. I lost in three seconds.
If the world really ends when the grand stone calendar rolls over, does that mean bedtime is canceled?
I made a leaf crown! Now bow before your supreme jungle emperor... or give me a cookie, whichever is easier.
Watch out for the vines with red berries! They don't taste good and your tongue turns blue for a week.
I hid my favorite obsidian pebble under a step of the main temple. Please don't tell the high priest!
My uncle says if you stand under a cocoa tree long enough, a monkey will drop money on your head.
I tried to dance the rain dance to get out of doing my chores, but it just flooded the kitchen instead.
Is it true people in other biomes wear clothes made of sheep hair? That sounds super itchy!
I tried to paint my face like a ferocious jaguar, but it just looks like I spilled berry juice everywhere.
The high priest said I have a pure heart! That's good, right? He kept eyeing my chest though...
My dad says obsidian blades are for sacred rituals, but they cut jungle melons way better than bronze.
I fell into a temple dart trap yesterday. Good news: I dodged all the arrows! Bad news: I ruined my loincloth.
I'm saving up twenty cocoa beans to buy a wooden carved ocelot. I only need nineteen more!
Grandma says the jungle spirits hear everything we say, so I apologized to the bush I accidentally tripped over.
My brother told me if I lie on the ceremonial altar during an eclipse, I get free candy. He's lying, right?
I tried to ride a wild tapir earlier. The tapir was not informed of this plan.
If I get chosen as a sacrifice to the rain god, do I still have to do my math homework tomorrow?
Look at this cool skull I found by the cenote! It's missing a tooth, just like me!
I asked the iron golem if he wanted to play tag. He didn't answer, but he tagged me into the next chunk.

cookie_success: Mmmm! Pure sweet cocoa magic! The Sun God himself couldn't have baked a better cookie!
A cookie?! For me?! May the gods rain blessed rainfall upon your crops forever!
WOAH! Crunchy chocolatey heaven! I'm never washing my hands again so I can smell this forever!
cookie_fail_1: Hey! That's just a clump of dry mud shaped like a disc! You can't fool a jungle kid!
Are you trying to feed me dried monkey food? Hand over real chocolate or I'm telling the priest!
That smells like swamp algae... even the temple rats wouldn't eat this!
cookie_fail_2: First you offer a fake snack, and now you won't even share? May your next cocoa cup be lukewarm!
No cookie?! Fine! I hope a macaw poops on your helmet while you sleep!
You're holding out on me?! I'm gonna go tell the iron golem you called his nose flat!
sugar_rush: SPEED OF THE JAGUAR! SUN GOD POWER! I CAN RUN ALL THE WAY TO THE MOUNTAIN PYRAMID AND BACK IN TWO SECONDS!
WOOOOOAH MY HEART IS BEATING LIKE A SACRED WAR DRUM! I CAN SEE COLOURS THAT DON'T EVEN EXIST YET!
SUGAR! SUGAR! SUGAR! I'M GONNA CLIMB THE BIGGEST BAMBOO TREE AND JUMP ONTO A PARROT!
sugar_fail: Ugh... my tummy feels like a volcanic eruption... why is the jungle spinning around?!
I think my teeth are vibrating... my mom is gonna sacrifice me to the bath tub when she sees this...
Blegh... too much sugar... the spirits are whispering, and they're telling me to sit down before I barf...
toy_success: A real carved wooden ocelot?! WOAH! It has tiny painted spots and everything! You're the best traveler ever!
Is this a real jade whistle?! *FIIIIII* Hahaha! I'm gonna annoy the temple guard all afternoon!
A mini ritual ball?! Now I can practice my hip-strikes without breaking mom's clay pots!
toy_fail: This is literally just a stick. I have a hundred sticks outside my hut. Give me something cool!
You call this a toy? My baby cousin wouldn't even play with this broken piece of vine!
That looks like something the high priest discarded after a ritual... no thank you!
parents: My dad's at the quarry cutting giant stone slabs for the new pyramid. He said if I touch his chisel, I'm grounded until the next century!
Mom is at the market trading woven feathers for cocoa. She told me to stay here and not join any cults.
My parents are at the temple praying for rain. I tried to help by splashing water on them, but they didn't appreciate it.
rps_win: HA! Obsidian cuts Leaf! I win! The Sun God smiles upon my tactical genius!
YES! Rock smashes Scissors! In your face, traveler! I claim victory for the jungle!
Boom! My Golden Eagle beats your paper! You owe me a cocoa bean!
rps_lose: What?! Your Rock crushed my Obsidian Knife?! That stone must be enchanted!
Nooo! Paper covered my Sacred Rock?! How does flat paper even hurt a rock?!
Aw man! You beat me! The jungle calendar clearly predicted my defeat today...
rps_tie: Double Obsidian! It's a draw! We are equally blessed by the gods of combat!
Both paper?! Looks like we both wrapped the exact same ceremonial gift!
Two Rocks! We're just two stone heads staring at each other. Go again!
